summary: Both gates are correctly rung 3 (a predicate over the tree, not an agent instruction), both are wired into .pre-commit-config.yaml with always_run, both propagate exit status through finish(), and neither violates check-gate-scope.sh (git diff is git-derived, which is what the rule is about; using it instead of scoped_files to judge LINES is outside the rule, not a breach of it). No object-store request rate is touched by this change, so non-negotiable 6 is not in play. Two majors block. (1) GATE_SCOPE=full is a no-op in both scripts and neither prints its mode, yet the same commit ships a backlog row (M0.77) telling a future session that check-test-inventory-claims.sh 'finds ~19 pre-existing assertion inventories in full mode'; I ran exactly that and it printed 'ok 0 added comment line(s) in tests, none an assertion inventory' over a tree containing 49 matching comment lines in 31 files. (2) check-archive-row-size.sh recognises a row only as the literal prefix '+| M'; a 6027-char row written as '|  M9.2 |' or '|M9.3 |' passes with 'ok 0 archive row(s) added', while the sibling gate it extends, check-session-load.sh, parses the same row with ^\|\s*(M-?\d+\.\d+[a-z]?)\s*\|. Minors: added-lines-only grandfathering is defeated by a pure line MOVE (verified), the '~19 files' figure is not reproducible, the length is locale-dependent and off by one, and neither gate has the negative-control harness test that BacklogBoundsTest gives the sibling cap.

findings.title: GATE_SCOPE=full is a no-op in both gates, neither prints its mode, and a committed backlog row prescribes a 'full mode' that returns ok over 49 violations
findings.detail:
lib.sh states the contract: 'Every gate PRINTS its mode. A delta pass is a weaker statement than a full pass and must not read like one -- non-negotiable 4.' Neither new gate calls scope_note(), and neither branches on GATE_SCOPE at all: both resolve CHECK_RANGE or fall back to git diff --cached, so GATE_SCOPE=full changes nothing. Reproduced on a clean checkout of HEAD with the two staged scripts overlaid and nothing staged:

  $ GATE_SCOPE=full ./scripts/check-test-inventory-claims.sh
  check-test-inventory-claims
    ok   0 added comment line(s) in tests, none an assertion inventory
  exit=0

The same tree contains 49 comment lines matching the gate's own PATTERN across 31 *Test.java files (buildSrc 5, format 6, ingest 3, sequencer 17). The success line does not disclose that it examined nothing.

Concrete failure scenario, and it is written into this commit rather than hypothetical: the M0.77 row added to backlog.md says 'SWEEP THE ~19 PRE-EXISTING ASSERTION INVENTORIES that check-test-inventory-claims.sh finds in full mode'. A session picking up M0.77 runs the gate in full mode, gets 'ok 0 ... none an assertion inventory', and closes the row as already clean. The script header repeats the same claim ('A full sweep flags ~19 files of text that predates this gate') for a sweep the script cannot perform.

Second scenario, CI: ci.yml sets GATE_SCOPE=full precisely because 'the delta path selects from a staged diff, and a fresh checkout has nothing staged, so every one would print ok over an empty set'. These two gates are the exception it warns about; they survive today only because ci.yml also exports CHECK_RANGE. That same ci.yml block carries the comment 'CHECK_RANGE is carried but currently drives NOTHING that runs here', which this commit makes false and does not update. Acting on that comment and dropping the env var silently returns both gates to the empty-staged-diff path with a green ok.

Also not reproducible: the '~19 files' figure appears in three committed places (the M0.76 archive row, the M0.77 backlog row, this script's header). Measured against the gate's own regex, restricted to lines containing // or *, it is 31 files / 49 lines; no subset of directories yields 19. Non-negotiable 4 governs numbers stated as measured.

Remedy: either implement the full branch (workspace_files '*Test.java' '*Tests.java' under GATE_SCOPE=full, which is what M0.77 needs to be actionable), or make both gates say what they did not look at -- and correct the count wherever it is stated.
findings.failure_scenario: A session picks up the M0.77 row added by this same commit, runs `GATE_SCOPE=full scripts/check-test-inventory-claims.sh` as the row instructs, sees `ok 0 added comment line(s) in tests, none an assertion inventory`, and closes M0.77 as already clean -- while 49 matching comment lines remain across 31 *Test.java files. Separately, someone acting on ci.yml's now-false comment that CHECK_RANGE 'drives NOTHING that runs here' removes the env var, and both gates fall back to `git diff --cached` in a fresh CI checkout, which is empty, printing ok over nothing on every run.

findings.title: check-archive-row-size.sh fails open on any row not written as exactly '| M', and reports it as 'ok 0 archive row(s) added'
findings.detail:
Row detection is `case "$line" in '+| M'*) ;; *) continue ;;` -- a literal pipe, one space, capital M. Constructed the input the gate must reject, per gate-design step 2, in a scratch clone of HEAD with the staged script:

  A  '| M9.1 | <6000 chars> | -- | **done** |'  -> FAIL row M9.1 is 6027 chars, cap 4000   exit=1
  B  '|  M9.2 | <6000 chars> | -- | **done** |' -> ok 0 archive row(s) added            exit=0
  C  '|M9.3 | <6000 chars> | -- | **done** |'   -> ok 0 archive row(s) added            exit=0
  D  '| R9.4 | <6000 chars> | -- | **done** |'  -> ok 0 archive row(s) added            exit=0

B and C are valid GitHub-flavoured markdown and render identically to A. The gate this one extends already solves the same parse correctly: check-session-load.sh uses ROW = ^\|\s*(M-?\d+\.\d+[a-z]?)\s*\| in its python block. Two definitions of 'a backlog row' now live in this repository and only the new one fails open.

This is the vacuous-pass shape the review lens names: the success line 'ok 0 archive row(s) added' is byte-identical whether no row was added or a 6000-char row was added and not parsed. A pre-commit run showing 0 next to a commit that plainly adds a row is the only signal, and nobody reads it that way.

Remedy: reuse check-session-load.sh's ROW regex (grep -E '^\+\|[[:space:]]*M-?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+[a-z]?[[:space:]]*\|'), and cross-check the parsed count against the number of added table lines so an unparsed row is a FAIL rather than a zero.
findings.failure_scenario: An author adds an over-cap archive row written as '|  M9.9 | ... |' (two spaces, valid markdown, renders identically). check-archive-row-size.sh prints `ok 0 archive row(s) added, each within 4000 chars` and exits 0, so a 6027-char row lands with the gate green -- verified against a scratch clone of HEAD with the staged script. The same row written with one space is correctly rejected, so the failure is invisible to anyone who only tested the canonical shape.

findings.title: 'added lines only' grandfathering is defeated by a pure MOVE, and both headers claim otherwise
findings.detail:
check-archive-row-size.sh's header states 'This gate judges only what a change ADDS, so legacy rows stay untouched and the exemption stops being a licence.' That is true only while git never re-renders a legacy line as added. Verified it does: moving the untouched 11,481-char M4.9 row to the end of backlog-done.md, changing no character of it, produces

  FAIL docs/internal/product/backlog-done.md: row M4.9 is 11482 chars, cap 4000 -- summarise it and put the essay in backlog-notes.md

i.e. the gate demands a rewrite of a shipped row, which is exactly the outcome the archive exemption exists to prevent. (A 3-to-4-column normalisation of the M0.10/M0.11/M0.12 rows stays under the cap and passes, so the hazard is specific to the 25 legacy rows already over 4000.)

This mechanism is already measured in this repository: review.md's `two-round-cap` records that for baselines/review.txt, '"ADDED" means "git renders it as an added line", so an edit that re-renders an already-committed argument as added re-arms it. Measured, not yet fixed: M4.31.' Same mechanism, opposite direction, and the new headers assert its absence.

Failure scenario: a future session reorganises backlog-done.md by milestone -- ordinary maintenance -- and 25 over-cap legacy rows re-render as added. The routes out are ARCHIVE_ROW_CAP=99999 (leaves no trace in the tree) or --no-verify (which also disables check-reviewed and check-tdd, neither of which CI can re-run). That is precisely 'a gate that fails CI on legacy is a gate someone turns off', arrived at by a different path than the one the design guards. check-test-inventory-claims.sh has the same exposure over 49 lines and no env escape at all, so its only route is --no-verify.

Remedy is a sentence, not code: state the blind spot honestly (gate-design step 5) -- 'a MOVE re-arms this' -- and, if an escape is wanted, make it a staged line in a tree file the way review.md's rounds: escape is, rather than an env var.
findings.failure_scenario: A future session reorganises backlog-done.md by milestone, changing no character of any legacy row. git re-renders the moved rows as added and the gate fails on 25 rows already over the cap, demanding they be rewritten -- verified by moving the untouched M4.9 row, which produced `FAIL row M4.9 is 11482 chars`. The routes out are ARCHIVE_ROW_CAP=99999, which leaves no trace in the tree, or --no-verify, which also disables check-reviewed and check-tdd, neither of which CI can re-run.

findings.title: the escape hatches are the wrong way round: the size cap is silently overridable, the false-positive-prone regex has no escape
findings.detail:
ARCHIVE_ROW_CAP is overridable by env, which matches the existing convention (BACKLOG_ROW_CAP, LAYER0_CAP) so it is not a new defect on its own -- but an env override leaves nothing in the tree, and non-negotiable 2 applies to this threshold like any other. Meanwhile check-test-inventory-claims.sh, the gate that will actually produce false refusals, has no escape.

Measured false-refusal rate over real material (gate-design step 3): of the 49 matching lines, 6 are class-level Javadoc stating a file's convention rather than counting assertions elsewhere -- 'EVERY test here has a deadline' (DefaultIngestTest, StreamingAppendTest), 'EVERY TEST HERE EXISTS BECAUSE A MUTATION SURVIVED' (CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest), 'EVERY TEST HERE EXISTS BECAUSE REVIEW MEASURED THE HANG IT PREVENTS' (BatchingSequencerLifecycleTest), 'every test here is about who may sequence and for how long' (LeaseManagerTest), 'Every test here injects its ...' (LocalSequencerRenewTest). For these the gate's remedy message -- 'state the PROPERTY instead' -- has no referent; there is no assertion being counted. ~12% of hits, and the shape recurs, since it is how this codebase writes a test-class Javadoc.

Failure scenario: an author writes an accurate class Javadoc of that shape, the gate refuses, and with no argued-escape route the cheapest fix is --no-verify, which drops check-reviewed and check-tdd for that commit. Either narrow the third alternation (require a comparative context rather than any 'every test here'), or give the gate a staged, traceable waiver.

Blind spots worth stating in the header while you are there: the gate sees only *Test.java / *Tests.java (56 other .java files under src/test and 5 under src/testFixtures are invisible -- none match today), and it recognises exactly four sentence shapes, so 'all other tests', 'the only place', 'the rest of the suite' and 'all 294 tests pass' pass unmatched.
findings.failure_scenario: An author writes an accurate class Javadoc of the shape this codebase already uses six times -- 'EVERY test here has a deadline' -- and check-test-inventory-claims.sh refuses it with a remedy ('state the PROPERTY instead') that has no referent, because no assertion is being counted. With no argued-escape route for that gate, the cheapest fix is --no-verify, which drops check-reviewed and check-tdd for that commit. Meanwhile the cap that the task's own row says was overridden under pressure is silently overridable by ARCHIVE_ROW_CAP with nothing recorded in the tree.

findings.title: the archive row length is locale-dependent and includes the diff's '+', while the cap it is compared against is defined in characters
findings.detail:
n=${#line} is measured on the diff line including its leading '+', and bash counts characters or bytes depending on LC_CTYPE. On the M0.76 row now staged: 1384 characters, 1402 bytes; LC_ALL=C bash reports 1402, C.UTF-8 reports 1384. The archive rows are dense with multibyte glyphs (WARNING sign, em dash, arrow), so the gap grows with the rows the gate targets -- the M4.9 row is reported as 11482 where the backlog says 11,481.

The error is conservative (bytes >= chars, plus one), so it can only fail closed, never open. What it costs is determinism: a row near the cap can fail on a machine with LC_ALL=C and pass on the next one, and the message says 'chars' for a number that is sometimes bytes. This repository has already been bitten by a gate whose verdict depended on the developer's environment (check-gate-scope.sh's record of the ~/.config/git/ignore false pass). The sibling cap in check-session-load.sh measures with python len(), i.e. characters, so the two caps are currently in different units.

Remedy: strip the '+' and count with the same primitive the sibling gate uses, or say 'bytes' and set the cap in bytes.
findings.failure_scenario: An archive row of 3,990 characters containing 40 multibyte glyphs measures 4,010 bytes. It passes pre-commit on a C.UTF-8 machine and fails on a machine or hook environment running LC_ALL=C, reporting '4010 chars' for a row that is 3,990 characters -- a verdict that depends on the developer's locale rather than on the repository, and a number the message mislabels. The sibling cap in check-session-load.sh counts characters via python len(), so the two caps disagree on the unit.

findings.title: neither gate ships the negative-control harness test that every comparable gate in this repository has
findings.detail:
Noted as production risk rather than test coverage, and it overlaps the test-reviewer's lane. buildSrc/src/test/java/binjava/ has tests for check-session-load, check-file-size, check-module, check-terminology, check-rule-citations, check-commit-msg, check-test-integrity, check-reviewed, check-gate-scope and more. BacklogBoundsTest -- the test for the 600-char cap this new 4000-char cap is the sibling of -- states the reason directly: 'each test carries its own negative control, because a bound with no counter-case is indistinguishable from a gate that refuses everything.'

These two gates add 98 lines of enforcement with no such test, and check-tdd passed vacuously because the diff adds no test file. F2 is the concrete cost: a positive control ('| M9.1 |' over cap fails) and a negative control ('| M9.1 |' under cap passes) both hold, while the one case in between -- a row the parser does not recognise -- was never constructed, and it fails open. A parse test over the row shapes the archive actually contains would have caught it.

Without a test, both scripts are also invisible to check-harness-tests.sh, so a later edit that breaks the regex is caught by nothing.
findings.failure_scenario: A later edit narrows or breaks either regex -- for example someone 'simplifies' the archive gate's case pattern -- and nothing fails: no harness test covers either script, so check-harness-tests.sh sees them not at all and the gate silently stops matching. F2 is that failure already present at birth: positive and negative controls both hold, and the unrecognised-row case in between was never constructed.
